selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What does the speaker say the palace owner wants people to do first in response to the palace and its displays?
questions.answer: They should recognize the owner and try to know him.

questions.question: How should admiration for the palace move beyond simple enjoyment?
questions.answer: It should become appreciation of the maker and affection for him.

questions.question: What do the unique marks on each work show about the owner?
questions.answer: They show that everything belongs to him alone and comes directly from him.

questions.question: What truth about the owner’s uniqueness should the audience accept?
questions.answer: That he stands alone, without any partner or equal.

questions.question: What question made the first group search for deeper meaning?
questions.answer: They wondered what hidden secret and meaning lay behind what they were seeing.

questions.question: Why did they believe the instructor was the right person to ask?
questions.answer: They understood that he possessed the explanation they needed.

questions.question: What reward did the first group receive?
questions.answer: They were invited to a higher, special palace and given lasting happiness there.

questions.question: What had gone wrong inside the second group before they even acted outwardly?
questions.answer: Their thinking and hearts were already damaged.

questions.question: What mistake did they make with the drinks?
questions.answer: They drank special mixtures meant for another use, not for ordinary drinking.

questions.question: What two public wrongs followed from that choice?
questions.answer: They became drunk and loudly disturbed everyone else.

questions.question: In the instructor’s announcement, what is the main purpose of the palace owner in showing the palace to the people?
questions.answer: He wants to make himself known to them.

questions.question: How are people told to answer the owner’s desire to be loved?
questions.answer: They should make themselves beloved through valuing his works.

questions.question: What do the owner’s personal marks on every crafted thing prove?
questions.answer: They prove exclusive ownership and authorship.

questions.question: What must people affirm about that owner once they understand those signs?
questions.answer: That he is one, unique, and has no equal.

questions.question: What led them to see the instructor as essential?
questions.answer: They understood that he held the explanation of the hidden meanings.

questions.question: How did they know where to turn for answers?
questions.answer: They realized the instructor held the explanation of the mysteries.

questions.question: What inward condition made the second group fail from the beginning?
questions.answer: Their minds were morally spoiled and their hearts were spiritually deadened.

questions.question: What inner condition ruined the second group’s response?
questions.answer: Their minds were corrupt and their hearts were spiritually extinguished.

questions.question: How did their actions affect others in the palace?
questions.answer: They disturbed the other guests.

questions.question: What social harm came from their later behavior?
questions.answer: They disrupted the peace of the other guests.

questions.question: What is the first duty the instructor gives the people regarding the palace owner?
questions.answer: To recognize him and seek real knowledge of him.

questions.question: What is the right emotional response to the owner’s displayed beauty and generosity?
questions.answer: To love him.

questions.question: Why does the instructor mention a special stamp, seal, and sign on every work?
questions.answer: To show that every work points back to one sole maker.

questions.question: What view of the owner’s nature does the instructor urge the people to accept?
questions.answer: That he is absolutely unique and incomparable.

title: Parable Invitation by the Explaining Master and Conduct of the Two Groups
